title: Dark Chocolate Ice Cream
description: Deep, bittersweet chocolate ice cream made with 92% cacao chocolate, a rich light-cream base, and just enough cinnamon to give it a subtle Mexican-hot-chocolate character.
totalTime: Overnight chilling plus churning and freezing
ingredients: 100 g whole egg (about 2 large eggs, without shells)
100 g 92% cacao dark chocolate, finely chopped
steps: Whisk the eggs until light and slightly foamy, then gradually whisk in the sugar until fully combined.
Warm the light cream and whole milk over medium-low heat. Add the chopped 92% chocolate and stir until completely melted and smooth.
Slowly whisk some of the warm chocolate mixture into the egg-and-sugar mixture to temper the eggs, then return everything to the saucepan.
Cook gently, stirring constantly, until the base reaches 170°F (77°C). Do not boil.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla, salt, and cinnamon.
Cover and chill completely, preferably overnight.
Churn according to your ice cream maker’s instructions, then transfer to a container and freeze until firm.
notes: The 165 g sugar is intentional: it balances the bitterness of the 92% cacao chocolate. Keep the cinnamon subtle; it should register as a warm undertone rather than obvious cinnamon. The original discussion did not preserve the exact chocolate-bar weight, so 100 g is the house baseline within the 85–115 g range we had discussed.
